summary: What actually runs at the end of Part 2: the same two Next.js apps and one serverless function, with no new runtime node. What changed is that the rules now fail a build.

nodes.label: Reader
nodes.purpose: A blog reader who lands on the public site to learn about Bullpen, and can now read its architecture page.

nodes.label: Player
nodes.purpose: Opens the trading app to see live prices. Paper trades arrive in Part 4.

nodes.label: Bullpen Landing
nodes.purpose: The public landing site (apps/landing). Part 2 adds the /architecture page, which reads the repo's own records: the ADRs, the ADL, the CALM moments and the rules snapshot.

nodes.label: Bullpen Trading App
nodes.purpose: The trading app (apps/web) where players view live prices and will place paper trades.

nodes.label: Price Snapshot Service
nodes.purpose: Serverless function backing GET /api/price/[symbol] in apps/web; fetches a point-in-time price for a symbol from CoinGecko and returns it to the trading app. It is the only code that reads the CoinGecko Demo API key.

nodes.label: CoinGecko
nodes.purpose: CoinGecko's free Demo API (api.coingecko.com), called for BTC-USD price snapshots. Chosen after a Coinbase-based design was ruled out by Coinbase's Terms of Use.

steps.caption: Ask for a quote
steps.detail: The trading app requests a live BTC-USD snapshot.

steps.caption: Fetch upstream
steps.detail: Server-side call to CoinGecko, Demo API key in a header, never the URL.

steps.caption: Return the snapshot
steps.detail: Bullpen's own shape: symbol, price, changePercent, time, source, fetchedAt.
